dedupe_keys.name: multiscale remote sensing and ground truth dataset for mine waste characterisation at memi mine cyprus m4mining

description: This dataset from the Horizon Europe m4mining project documents mine waste at the legacy Memi Mine in the Republic of Cyprus, a volcanogenic massive sulphide deposit of the Troodos Ophiolite, from a field campaign in April 2024. It was published by Ekaterina Savinova, Friederike Koerting, Daniel Schläpfer and colleagues to support research on mine waste characterisation, environmental monitoring and hyperspectral remote sensing methods. It combines drone-mounted hyperspectral imaging in the visible, near-infrared and shortwave infrared, LiDAR and a digital surface model, handheld spectroradiometer measurements, X-ray diffraction and fluorescence analyses, ground control points and photographs, with a report on acquisition and processing. Version 1.0 (9 September 2026) is a free Zenodo download under CC-BY-4.0; the reflectance imagery alone is about 10.9 GB and the digital surface model about 97 MB. Caveats: it is a single site and date, intended as a methods test bed, not an inventory. For simulation it is calibration and validation data for remote sensing of tailings and waste dumps, supporting condition assessment and environmental impact models of legacy mine sites. Related catalogue records include the global mining polygons of Maus et al. and the WAPHA global metal mines database.
